P1-04.title: Batch-rename logic
P1-04.summary:
Branch port/P1-04 is committed with the Port-Stage trailer, and the worktree is detached. Both gates pass: `tools/parity/gen.sh --check` (26 suites up to date) and `scripts/ci.sh` (build, test with 499 passing, format).
Added `Sources/FTFoundation/BatchRename/`, with settings and types, `proposeNames`, `planBatchRename` (number, skip, block), saved-settings and preset sanitizers, and `JSRegExp`.
`JSRegExp` runs JavaScript unicode-mode regexes on `NSRegularExpression` after translating the pattern. It rewrites `$`, `.`, `\d \w \s \b`, named groups and literals so ICU's case folding matches JavaScript's.
The sanitizers are wired into `BatchRenameSanitizers.standard` in `PreferencesSanitizer.swift`, and `.passthrough` now points at it.
Goldens `batch-rename-propose` (600 cases, 2.7 MB) and `batch-rename-plan` (300 cases, 1.5 MB) both pass. A separate 322-case regex fuzz found a few differences, listed below. I used it to find them and did not commit it.
The 58 tests from `shared/batchRename.test.ts` are ported, plus the planning half of the 9 `batchRenamePlanAndRun` tests, each with its T-id. The run half is P3-08.

After merging, the integrator runs `bun tools/parity-matrix/sync.ts` to pick up the T-ids cited in `Tests/FTFoundationTests/BatchRename/BatchRenameTests.swift`. I did not touch `docs/port/parity/`.
deviations: The pattern-error text after 'The pattern isn’t valid: ' is this port's own wording, not V8's or JavaScriptCore's. The goldens compare only the prefix; whether a pattern is an error matches the reference on every pattern tested.

A few regex edge cases still differ from JavaScript and are documented on `JSRegExp`. They are: a back reference to a group that took no part, which fails here but matches the empty string in JavaScript; `\P{Lu}` under the `i` flag; the captures of empty loops such as `(a*)*` and `(|a)+`; look-behinds that are not of bounded length; and a ligature such as ﬁ inside a character class also matching 'fi'.
A saved text setting cut at 255 UTF-16 units inside a surrogate pair leaves U+FFFD here, where JavaScript keeps half the pair, because a Swift String cannot hold a lone surrogate.
The reference runs on Bun's JavaScriptCore, not V8, so the goldens record JSC's regex behaviour. The two engines are not known to differ on the tested patterns, but I did not check against V8.
The golden JSON files are large (4.2 MB together).

findings.title: Log context objects: key order and key quoting differ from util.inspect({sorted:true})
findings.where: Sources/FTFileSystem/Logging/LogFormat.swift (inspect, inspectKey) vs apps/desktop/src/main/appLog.ts formatArgs (inspect options: sorted, compact, breakLength Infinity)
findings.evidence: Node sorts the rendered entry strings, not the raw keys, and quotes any key that is not /^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*$/. The port sorts raw keys (LogFormat.swift, `members.keys.sorted()`), treats `$` and non-ASCII letters as bare identifiers (inspectKey, `$0 == "$" || $0.properties.isAlphabetic`), and puts no quote character first in the sort. I ran the reference with `node -e 'const {inspect}=require("util");console.log(inspect({a:1,a1:2,"a-b":3,b:4,$x:5},{depth:8,breakLength:Infinity,compact:true,sorted:true}))'`. It prints `{ '$x': 5, 'a-b': 3, a1: 2, a: 1, b: 4 }`. The port's algorithm gives `{ a: 1, a-b: ... }`: raw-key sort gives a, a-b, a1, b, $x. It also writes `$x` unquoted and `a-b` with the wrong quoting or order. Keys such as `a`/`a1` order differently because ':' (0x3a) sorts after digits in the rendered `key: value` strings. The same applies to `$`-prefixed and quoted keys, which sort first because of the leading quote. Writing structured entries (`write(level:namespace:message:context:)`) with such context keys gives a different app.log line than the reference. No test covers this: Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Logging/AppLoggerTests.swift has no `sorted` or inspect-ordering case. Reproduce the port side with a Swift test calling `LogFormat.arguments([.context(["a":.number(1),"a1":.number(2),"$x":.number(5)])])` and comparing to `{ '$x': 5, a1: 2, a: 1 }`.
